text:
Anya (Product): quick sync — we need to align on the long-term routing playbook for geo + multi-tenant isolation. Customer asks are piling up and sales wants launch criteria by EOW
Sanjay (Eng): +1. can we scope options first? i see 3 paths: strict tenant lanes, soft-eviction with fallbacks, or policy-driven routing (per-tenant rules). each has different infra/cost impact
Meera (Arch): listing tradeoffs: strict lanes = best isolation & predictable perf but big capacity headroom. soft-evict = cheaper but adds complexity in drain/evac logic. policy-driven = flexible but will need a robust policy-eval plane (latency risk)
Kevin (Sales): customers care about two things: SLA isolation (no noisy neighbor) and predictable pricing. a few will pay for dedicated lanes, most want a cheaper shared option with guarantees
Eli (SRE): operational checklist: autoscale granularity, cross-region failover, and telemetry per-tenant. also need evacuation playbook + runbooks for partial region failures (we saw the choke points in the last DR test)
Anya (Product): what would be reasonable launch criteria for an MVP of the shared-with-fallback model? product needs: clear SLA buckets, documented rollback, and migration plan for existing tenants
Sanjay (Eng): propose MVP acceptance: 1) routing policy proto that supports per-tenant priority and region preference, 2) fallback chain defined (model variant -> region -> capacity tier), 3) perf guardrail that aborts routes exceeding 200ms extra latency
Meera (Arch): add acceptance: KV-cache affinity must be observable and evictable per-tenant. also require deterministic eviction order for soft-eviction so we can explain behavior to customers
Kevin (Sales): also need a sales-facing matrix: when customer chooses "isolation-boost" what do they get (SLA, cost delta, migration ETA). Without that, leads stall
Eli (SRE): small ops ask: we need a canary path and a traffic mirror for first 30 customers. mirror ~5% traffic to new routing path for 2 weeks before cutover
Sanjay (Eng): engineering trade: policy-eval can be centralized (simpler) or pushed to edge nodes (lower latency). central = simpler rollout, edge = better tail latency. which do we prefer?
Meera (Arch): prefer hybrid: central control plane for policies, edge fast-eval cache with TTLs. requirement: policy changes must be consistent within 10s globally
Anya (Product): timeline asks: if we do hybrid, what effort? rough estimate?
Sanjay (Eng): rough: spike (2w) to validate edge eval cache and policy distribution, core impl (8w) for routing rules + fallbacks, tests & canaries (4w). total ~14w for MVP
Kevin (Sales): can we break into milestones for customers? spike -> private beta -> general availability. sales needs private beta slots by week 10 ideally
Meera (Arch): dependency list: model-variant registry API, cross-region KV routing metadata, telemetry tags per-tenant, and rollout automation for policies. missing any and we block the path
Eli (SRE): and infra gating: we need an SLA-backed capacity pool option (dedicated lanes) implemented as part of the bigger program; otherwise we hand customers a half-solution
Anya (Product): prioritization question: should we build dedicated lanes first (big customer revenue) or shared-with-fallback (broader adoption)? leaning toward shared-first with a clear path to dedicated lanes
Kevin (Sales): pragmatic: ship shared-first, but lock in a paid "upgrade path" for customers ready for dedicated lanes. they want clear SLAs and a migration window (30-90d)
Sanjay (Eng): implementation note: routing config should be a first-class resource (policy-as-config). store in versioned service so rollbacks are easy. example config snippet we can use in spike:
```
route: {
  tenant: "acct-123",
  priority: "high",
  region_pref: ["us-west-2","us-east-1"],
  fallbacks: ["model-lowq","region-fallback","dedicated-pool"]
}
```
Meera (Arch): ops-safety: include a hard circuit-breaker: global token rate cap per-tenant to stop runaway migration. and autoscale cooldowns so we don't thrash GPUs
Eli (SRE): monitoring: we need per-tenant SLOs for p50/p95 latency, token cost delta, and a migration health metric. alerts for >x% of requests hitting fallback chain
Anya (Product): action items: 1) Sanjay/Meera run 2w spike (policy distribution + edge cache) 2) Eli set up canary plan & telemetry schema 3) Kevin drafts sales matrix and upgrade SKUs 4) Anya draft MVP acceptance criteria doc
Sanjay (Eng): I'll own the spike. plan: deliver prototypes + perf numbers in 2w. will post daily standups in this thread
Meera (Arch): i'll pair on policy distribution + give a migration pattern for tenants (wave-based). will include cost estimates for strict lanes vs shared path
Eli (SRE): i'll mock the telemetry and run a dry-run failover test against staging region this week
Kevin (Sales): collecting a short list of customers who want to be private-beta early adopters. will share names by EOD
deploy-bot: deploy complete to staging: routing-playground v0.1 — tests passing (15/15) :rocket:
Anya (Product): thanks team. next sync Fri 10am. please add blockers here before EOD tomorrow
Sanjay (Eng): noted. first daily update: started spike, infra token for edge cache requested
Meera (Arch): added migration-wave draft to the shared drive, link: https://rwd.internal/drive/migration-wave-draft
Eli (SRE): staging failover dry-run scheduled for Thu 03:00 UTC
Kevin (Sales): sending customer invites for private beta next week
Anya (Product): perfect — holding product decision for final acceptance after canary results
Meera (Arch): one last note: let's avoid the term "soft-evict" in customer-facing docs; call it "graceful fallback" instead
Anya (Product): agreed. that phrasing will go into the sales matrix
Sanjay (Eng): ok wrapping up, will post perf numbers in 48h
Eli (SRE): will add runbook template to ops-runbooks repo
Anya (Product): end-of-thread recap: spike (2w) -> private beta (wk10) -> GA (~wk14) assuming no major perf regressions. owners assigned. :+1:
